bugs.title: find_duplicates overwrites the store, deleting duplicate and invalid records
bugs.expected: The stored records are not changed in any way; count() and all_transactions() return the same results before and after the call.
bugs.actual: Both failed. count() was 2 instead of 5 after the call (assert 2 == 5); all_transactions() differed from the snapshot taken before the call.
bugs.evidence: Line 54 `self._transactions = unique` replaces the store. For ids A, B, A, C the store shrinks from 4 records to 3; invalid records are dropped as well.

reproduction.result_before_fix: Both failed. count() was 2 instead of 5 after the call (assert 2 == 5); all_transactions() differed from the snapshot taken before the call.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: line 54 assigns the de-duplicated list of valid records back to self._transactions, so a read-only query replaces the store. Symptoms: count(), all_transactions(), get_transaction() and every calculation change after the first call; the CLI summary is only unaffected because it calls find_duplicates last.

fix.summary: Removed the line `self._transactions = unique` from find_duplicates so the method no longer writes to the store.

verification.full_suite: After this fix: 51 failed, 40 passed (was 53 failed, 38 passed); no previously passing test failed. Related run (-k duplicates): 6 failed, 3 passed, the 6 being BH-002 tests not yet fixed.

bugs.notes: Found by the orchestrator while performing the bug-scout role inline (code reading only, nothing run). The called-twice test was first filed here; it fails because of the wrong return value, so it was moved to BH-002 before any fix was made.

bugs.title: find_duplicates returns the first occurrences instead of the duplicates
bugs.expected: Returns every valid record whose id already appeared in an earlier valid record; the first record with an id is not returned. Ids A, B, A, C, A return the third and fifth records; no duplicates returns [].
bugs.expected_behaviour_source: demo-app/EXPECTED_BEHAVIOUR.md section find_duplicates(), first and second bullets and the example; tests/test_app.py::test_find_duplicates_returns_the_repeated_record
bugs.actual: All 6 failed. Ids A, B, A, C, A returned the first A, B and C records instead of the third and fifth; a store with no duplicates returned every record instead of []; the CLI printed 4 lines instead of 1 (assert 4 == 1). Two consecutive calls did not both return the one duplicate.
bugs.evidence: Lines 51-53 append a record to `unique` when its id has NOT been seen, and line 55 returns `unique`. For ids A, B, A, C it returns the A, B and C originals rather than the second A.

reproduction.result_before_fix: All 6 failed. Ids A, B, A, C, A returned the first A, B and C records instead of the third and fifth; a store with no duplicates returned every record instead of []; the CLI printed 4 lines instead of 1 (assert 4 == 1). Two consecutive calls did not both return the one duplicate.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: the loop condition is inverted for the purpose. It collects a record when its id has not been seen (the originals) and discards the later ones, then returns that list. Symptom: the CLI `duplicates` command lists 4 originals and `summary` reports 4 duplicates. Shares the function with BH-001 but is a separate wrong decision (what is returned versus what is stored).

fix.summary: find_duplicates now appends a record when its id is already in `seen` and otherwise records the id; the local list was renamed from `unique` to `duplicates` because it now holds the duplicates.

verification.targeted: 6 passed: the 6 reproduction tests listed under reproduction.test

bugs.title: get_transaction raises or returns the wrong record for an invalid index
bugs.expected: If index is not an integer, is negative, or is >= count(), returns None. Never raises.
bugs.actual: All failed (2 existing tests and 12 new test cases). IndexError for index 10, 99, count() and for 0 on an empty store; -1 and -2 returned records counted from the end; '1', 1.0, 1.5, None, [1] and (0,) raised TypeError.
bugs.evidence: Line 59 `return self._transactions[index]` is a bare list subscript: [10] on 4 records raises IndexError, [-1] returns the last record, ['1'] and [1.0] raise TypeError.

reproduction.result_before_fix: All failed (2 existing tests and 12 new test cases). IndexError for index 10, 99, count() and for 0 on an empty store; -1 and -2 returned records counted from the end; '1', 1.0, 1.5, None, [1] and (0,) raised TypeError.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: line 59 passes the caller's index straight to a list subscript, which has Python's semantics (negative indexes count from the end, out-of-range raises IndexError, non-integers raise TypeError) rather than the specified ones. Symptom: `python3 app.py show 99` ends in a traceback.

fix.summary: get_transaction returns None unless index is an int with 0 <= index < len(self._transactions); only then does it subscript the list.

bugs.actual: All failed (2 existing tests and 8 new test cases) with 'DID NOT RAISE ValueError' for 150, -10, 100.01, 101, 1000, -0.01, -1, inf, -inf and nan.

reproduction.result_before_fix: All failed (2 existing tests and 8 new test cases) with 'DID NOT RAISE ValueError' for 150, -10, 100.01, 101, 1000, -0.01, -1, inf, -inf and nan.

fix.summary: apply_discount raises ValueError('percent must be between 0 and 100') unless 0 <= percent <= 100, before computing. The chained comparison also rejects NaN, which is not between 0 and 100.

bugs.title: validate_transaction raises OverflowError for an integer amount too large for a float
bugs.expected: validate_transaction never raises; average_transaction_value never raises for a store that holds only dictionaries.
bugs.expected_behaviour_source: demo-app/EXPECTED_BEHAVIOUR.md section validate_transaction, last bullet (Never raises); section average_transaction_value(), second bullet
bugs.actual: All 3 new test cases failed with OverflowError: int too large to convert to float at utils.py:33.
bugs.evidence: Line 33 `math.isnan(amount)` converts an int to a C double; an int beyond the float range cannot be converted.

reproduction.result_before_fix: All 3 new test cases failed with OverflowError: int too large to convert to float at utils.py:33.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: line 33 calls math.isnan on any int; converting an int beyond the float range to a C double raises OverflowError. Secondary failures: valid_transactions(), average_transaction_value(), total_valid_transactions(), find_duplicates() and add_transaction() all call validate_transaction, so they raise too.

fix.summary: validate_transaction now checks finiteness through a small private helper, _is_finite, which calls math.isfinite and returns False on the OverflowError raised for an int that cannot be represented as a float. Such an amount is reported as 'amount must be finite'. Only OverflowError is caught.

verification.targeted: 3 passed: the 3 new test cases listed under reproduction.test
verification.full_suite: After this fix: 91 passed, 0 failed (was 3 failed, 88 passed); no previously passing test failed. Related run (-k 'validate or amounts or calculations'): 37 passed.

bugs.notes: Found by the orchestrator while performing the bug-scout role inline (code reading only, nothing run). Decision recorded for the user: the specification says an amount is an int or float that is finite and not zero, and also that validation and the average never raise. An int such as 10**400 cannot take part in the float arithmetic the calculations use, so accepting it would break the 'never raises' rule for average_transaction_value. The proposed fix rejects it with the existing 'amount must be finite' problem. The regression tests assert only the sourced rule (nothing raises), not which way the record is classified.

bugs.title: average_transaction_value raises OverflowError when integer amounts sum beyond the float range and a float follows
bugs.expected: average_transaction_value never raises for a store that holds only dictionaries.
bugs.actual: Failed with OverflowError: int too large to convert to float at transaction_service.py:45 (the sum() line). Suite at that point: 1 failed, 92 passed.
bugs.evidence: Probe run after the BH-008 fix: a store with amounts 10**308, 10**308 and 1.5 (each valid on its own) made average_transaction_value raise OverflowError: int too large to convert to float, while total_valid_transactions returned inf without raising.

reproduction.result_before_fix: Failed with OverflowError: int too large to convert to float at transaction_service.py:45 (the sum() line). Suite at that point: 1 failed, 92 passed.

bugs.root_cause: Root cause: sum() starts from the int 0, so integer amounts accumulate as an arbitrary-precision int. Once that int is beyond the float range, adding the next float amount has to convert it and raises. total_valid_transactions does not have the problem because it accumulates from 0.0, where overflow gives inf instead of an exception. Symptom: the exception escapes average_transaction_value and the CLI summary.

fix.summary: Start the sum from 0.0 so the amounts accumulate as floats, the same way total_valid_transactions does.

bugs.notes: Found by the orchestrator while checking the neighbouring cases of BH-008 (the fix-review step of the test-engineer role, performed inline). Only reachable with integer amounts near 1e308.

observations.summary: get_transaction(True) / get_transaction(False): bool is a subclass of int in Python, so a bool index is treated as 1 / 0.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: The specification says only 'not an integer'. It excludes bool explicitly for amount but not for index, so whether a bool index should return None is a judgement call with no source.

observations.summary: `python3 app.py discount 200 150` has no specified output; once apply_discount raises ValueError as specified, the CLI will show a Python traceback for an out-of-range percent.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: The app.py table in the specification has no row for an invalid discount, so the expected CLI output is unspecified.

observations.summary: format_transaction would raise for a record whose amount is not a number (the :>10.2f format) or for a stored value that is not a dictionary.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: Not reachable with the built-in sample data, which is the only data the CLI loads; no specification row covers it.

observations.summary: load() stores the caller's dictionaries by reference, so later edits to the caller's dictionaries show in the store.
observations.reason_not_a_defect: The specification says load appends every record 'as given'; only add_transaction is specified to copy.
